article.body:
Mivtzoim—they feel like they’ve been around forever! Can you even imagine life without them? Yet, unbelievably, before the Rebbe introduced each of the mitzvah campaigns that we know so well, they simply didn’t exist.

Join us as we explore imaginary old diaries that could have belonged to kids just like you— kids who might have lived during the time when the Rebbe first announced many of these mivtzoim.

Most people didn’t pay attention to their birthdays, until the Rebbe changed all that. Join Simcha as he learns to celebrate his birthday … the Yiddishe way! )1988( כ"ה אדר, תשמ"ח

Tonight, over chicken and potatoes, Tatty said, “Kids, are you ready to hear something unbelievable that happened after shacharis today?”

Diary, I’m sure you know that since Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka was niftar, the Rebbe has been davening in his home with a smaller minyan. So anyways, Tatty goes to this minyan sometimes.

“It seemed like an ordinary morning,” began Tatty. “We finished shacharis, people were leaving for work, the Rebbe had already gone up to the second floor, I was folding up my tallis… Then, suddenly, everyone around me stopped what they were doing. I looked up, and I couldn’t believe my eyes.

At the Moshiach seuda on the last day of Pesach, the Rebbe spoke more about birthdays! The Rebbe showed us different places in the Torah that tell us about the importance of birthdays.

A couple of days ago, a proper organized list of all the birthday minhagim was given out, with ten different sections. The Rebbe himself edited it! I’m writing everything down with checkboxes so that when it’s my birthday, I won’t even miss one thing.

But Diary—don’t think Mivtza Yom Huledes is staying a secret! A full- page ad was published in the New York Times, which is a huge newspaper,

ALIYA Get an aliya on the Shabbos before your birthday. This one will have to wait. TZEDAKA Give extra tzedaka before shacharis and mincha. I put a whole load of coins into the pushka! TEFILLA Daven with extra kavana and say the whole Tehillim (or at least a sefer). I davened beautifully today! KAPITEL Learn and say your new kapitel. Yup!

saying “Birthdays Matter.” There was also a Yiddish ad in the Algemeiner Journal: “Do not miss out on observing the most important day of your life!” And more ads—too many to write down—were published all across the globe! I heard that in Eretz Yisroel there’s a full-blown campaign going on!

I heard that at dollars, the Rebbe sometimes even reminds children to have a party or a farbrengen in honor of their yom huledes! I can’t wait to go for dollars before my birthday!

It’s really special that keeping the minhagim of a Yom Huledes is a z’chus for the aliyas haneshema of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka. It makes Mivtza Yom Huledes extra special for us chassidim.

TORAH Learn extra Torah—both Niglah and Chassidus. I learned a few extra lines of Tanya Baal Peh, and Sefer Hamitzvos, too. MAAMAR Chazer a maamar (or part of a maamar) baal peh. I think I’ll do this when I’m a bit older. HAFATZA Encourage other people to grow in their Yiddishkeit and Chassidishkeit, even more than we usually do! I was feeling a bit shy, but I invited a neighbor to my birthday farbrengen so he could hear some

Chassidus and learn about mivtza yom huledes! HISBODEDUS Spend some time all alone thinking about the past year: what I did well, and what I need to do better next year. I did a great job sharing my Shabbos treats with my younger siblings. And I definitely need to stop talking so much in class. HIDDUR MITZVAH Do something even better than before! I took on a hachlata to say Asher Yatzar with more kavana for a whole month. I’ll do this by standing in one place when I say it.

I announced that to everyone at my farbrengen, so they can all help me remember to keep my hachlata! FARBRENGEN (My favorite one!) Have a farbrengen with family and friends to thank Hashem for this special day, take on hachlatos, and make a bracha ׁשֶהֶחֱיָנּו on a new fruit. You should have seen the seven-layer cake Mommy baked me … with the special fruit right on top!

“The Rebbe walked over to the shtender, and started saying a sicha!”

“What did the Rebbe say?” asked my older sister Shaina.

“Today is actually Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka’s birthday, and the Rebbe spoke

“Yes.” Tatty answered. “Would you believe it? I don’t know if Zeidy even knows when his birthday is. Wait—when’s mine again? Sometime after Pesach, no? Chof-vov, chof-zayin…?”

“It does say in the Hayom Yom for Yud-Alef Nissan that your birthday is a day of cheshbon hanefesh and teshuva,” my older brother pointed out. He always knows everything.

“Right,” Mommy said. "And there was a point some years ago where bochurim would have a yechidus on their birthdays, but no one really pays much attention to birthdays b’chlal! It’s more of a private, quiet thing.”

“Yes, that’s all going to change now!” chimed in Dovi.

“That’s right!” responded Tatty. “The Rebbe said that we should be celebrating our birthdays! We should make joyful Chassidishe farbrengens with friends and family, taking on new hachlatos, and doing extra mitzvos. Kids, too!”
